title: Foreign-born Asian Americans — spouse ethnicity (ACS)
definition: Among foreign-born Asian householders who are married with spouse present, the share whose spouse is the same Asian ethnicity (endogamy / intra-ethnic), another Asian ethnicity (interethnic), or a non-Asian (interracial). From ACS PUMS analysis limited to the foreign-born.
source: Yang, Philip Q., and Maggie Bohm-Jordan. 2018. “Patterns of Interracial and Interethnic Marriages among Foreign-Born Asians in the United States.” Societies 8(3): 87. Table 2, ACS 2008–2012 PUMS.
note: Foreign-born rates only — U.S.-born Asians intermarry far more (Pew: 46% of U.S.-born Asian newlyweds in 2015). Endogamy here is co-ethnic marriage, stricter than “any Asian spouse.” Across all foreign-born Asian householders, 88.8% married co-ethnics, 8.0% married non-Asians, and 3.3% married another Asian ethnicity.
